research_title: MedCode Clinical: platform design and benchmark evaluation
research_subtitle: An offline, explainable multi-vocabulary terminology retrieval system with reproducible quality assessment.
research_abstract_background: Clinical workflows depend on lookups across incompatible coding systems, yet most retrieval tools are proprietary, network-dependent, or opaque in ranking.
research_abstract_objective: To implement MedCode Clinical and evaluate whether transparent layered retrieval outperforms lexical SQLite search across eight biomedical coding schemes.
research_abstract_methods: We bundled twelve terminologies with provenance metadata and measured precision@1 and precision@5 on 82 curated queries, comparing layered retrieval (exact, prefix, substring, fuzzy, alias) with SQLite LIKE search.
research_abstract_results: Layered retrieval achieved mean precision@1 = 0.95 versus 0.71 for SQLite. Gains were largest on ICD-10-CM (+0.33) and LOINC (+0.60). Hebrew queries achieved precision@1 = 1.00 after Stage-A label import.
research_abstract_conclusions: Explainable layered retrieval improves top-rank precision while preserving auditability. Certified-coder validation is needed before production coding claims.
